Active recall beats passive re-reading: quiz yourself before checking the answer.
Spaced repetition works because forgetting is predictable — review right before you'd forget.
When a flashcard is easy, rate it honestly. Inflating your rating just delays the review you actually need.
Interleave subjects (e.g., cardio then pharm) instead of blocking one topic for hours — it improves long-term retention.
Explain the answer out loud in your own words before flipping the card. If you can't, you don't know it yet.
Missed a quiz question? Re-read the explanation, then write a one-line flashcard for it yourself.
Short, daily review sessions beat long, infrequent cramming sessions for retention.
Sleep consolidates memory — a review session right before bed can help lock in the day's learning.
Tag your hardest cards and drill them in a separate short session at the end of the day.
Test yourself under mild time pressure occasionally — it mimics exam conditions and improves recall speed.
